newsitem.title: GERMANY: Austria calls for generous reading of EMU rules.
newsitem.headline: Austria calls for generous reading of EMU rules.

text.p: Austrian Finance Minister Rudolf Edlinger on Wednesday called for a more generous reading of the entry rules for European monetary union (EMU), which he said leave room for interpretation.

In a German radio interview, Edlinger said the convergence criteria should be met, and that Austria would meet them. But the current pressure in Germany for a strict interpretation of the rules was misplaced, he said.
Edlinger said a delay of EMU would be dangerous, and that as many countries as possible should participate at the start.
The decisive factor is that budget deficits be moving "in the direction of three percent" of gross domestic product, the "reference value" contained in the Maastricht Treaty, he said.
"I believe that a discussion like the one going on now does not serve the matter," he said, adding that the euro should still be as stable and hard as possible.

Bavarian Premier Edmund Stoiber and German Chancellor Helmut Kohl on Tuesday apparently ended a long-festering feud when Kohl publicly bent to Stoiber's insistence that the EMU criteria be strictly met.
In a nod to the recent election of a left-wing government in France, Edlinger said the stability of the euro cannot be separated from the jobs situation.
"It is not a satisfactory solution if the 15 countries (of the European Union) have outstanding budgets but also have 20 million unemployed among them.
"I believe that the task of the next few years will be to work seriously to create more jobs in the EU," he said.
